meta.subject: other
meta.description: Social studies facts: communities, cultures, map skills, government basics, citizenship, economics basics, global awareness, current events literacy, world religions, human rights, United Nations

facts.statement: The five major world religions by number of followers are Christianity (~2.4 billion), Islam (~1.9 billion), Hinduism (~1.2 billion), Buddhism (~500 million), and Judaism (~15 million)
Monotheistic religions worship one God; Christianity, Islam, and Judaism are all monotheistic and share Abraham as a common patriarch
Hinduism is one of the world's oldest religions, originating in South Asia, and includes belief in many forms of the divine (Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva)
Buddhism was founded by Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha) in India around 500 BCE and teaches the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path to end suffering
The three Abrahamic religions (Judaism, Christianity, Islam) all originated in the Middle East and share common historical narratives
Freedom of religion is a fundamental human right recognized by the United Nations Universal Declaration of Human Rights
Sikhism was founded by Guru Nanak in the Punjab region of South Asia in the late 15th century; it is a monotheistic religion with about 30 million followers worldwide
Sacred texts include the Bible (Christianity), the Quran (Islam), the Torah (Judaism), the Vedas and Bhagavad Gita (Hinduism), and the Tripitaka (Buddhism)
A place of worship is called a church (Christianity), mosque (Islam), synagogue (Judaism), temple (Hinduism/Buddhism), or gurdwara (Sikhism)

common_errors.wrong: Islam is only practiced in the Middle East
common_errors.correct: Islam is practiced worldwide. The countries with the largest Muslim populations are Indonesia, Pakistan, India, and Bangladesh, all in South and Southeast Asia.

common_errors.wrong: Buddhism requires belief in a god
common_errors.correct: Buddhism focuses on personal spiritual development and does not require belief in a creator god. It centers on the Buddha's teachings about ending suffering.

common_errors.wrong: Hinduism has only one holy book
common_errors.correct: Hinduism has many sacred texts including the Vedas, Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, Ramayana, and Mahabharata.

common_errors.wrong: all religions worship the same way
common_errors.correct: Different religions have distinct practices: Christians may attend church services, Muslims pray five times daily facing Mecca, Buddhists meditate, and Hindus may worship at home shrines or temples.

facts.statement: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on December 10, 1948
The UDHR includes 30 articles covering civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights for all people
Human rights include the right to life, liberty, education, freedom of thought and religion, and freedom from slavery and torture
The US civil rights movement of the 1950s-1960s fought for racial equality, led by figures including Martin Luther King Jr., Rosa Parks, and John Lewis
Martin Luther King Jr. advocated for civil rights through nonviolent protest and civil disobedience, inspired by Mahatma Gandhi's philosophy
The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989) is the most widely ratified human rights treaty in history
The 19th Amendment to the US Constitution, ratified in 1920, granted women the right to vote
The Civil Rights Act of 1964 outlawed discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin in the United States
The 13th Amendment (1865) abolished slavery in the United States, and the 14th Amendment (1868) granted citizenship and equal protection under the law to all persons born in the US

common_errors.wrong: human rights were invented in the 20th century
common_errors.correct: While the UDHR was adopted in 1948, concepts of human rights have roots in ancient codes of law, the Magna Carta (1215), and Enlightenment philosophy.

common_errors.wrong: human rights are only about government actions
common_errors.correct: Human rights apply broadly and can be violated by governments, corporations, groups, and individuals. Protecting them is a shared responsibility.

common_errors.wrong: Martin Luther King Jr. was the only civil rights leader
common_errors.correct: The civil rights movement involved many leaders: Rosa Parks, Malcolm X, John Lewis, Medgar Evers, Fannie Lou Hamer, Thurgood Marshall, and many others.

common_errors.wrong: slavery only existed in the United States
common_errors.correct: Slavery existed in many civilizations throughout history, including ancient Rome, ancient Greece, the Middle East, Africa, Asia, and the Americas. The transatlantic slave trade was one of the most large-scale systems.

facts.statement: The United Nations was founded on October 24, 1945, after World War II, with the goal of maintaining international peace and security
The UN has 193 member states and is headquartered in New York City
The UN Security Council has 5 permanent members (US, UK, France, Russia, China) with veto power, and 10 non-permanent rotating members
UNICEF (United Nations Children's Fund) provides humanitarian aid and development assistance to children and mothers worldwide
UNESCO promotes international cooperation in education, science, culture, and communication
The UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are 17 global goals adopted in 2015 to be achieved by 2030, covering poverty, hunger, health, education, and climate action
The World Health Organization (WHO) is a UN agency responsible for international public health, coordinating responses to global health emergencies
UN peacekeeping missions deploy military and civilian personnel to help countries navigate the difficult transition from conflict to peace
The International Court of Justice (ICJ), located in The Hague, Netherlands, is the principal judicial organ of the UN that settles legal disputes between nations
The UN Secretary-General is the chief administrative officer of the United Nations; the position serves as a spokesperson and leader of the organization

common_errors.wrong: the UN is a world government
common_errors.correct: The UN is an international organization where sovereign nations cooperate voluntarily. It cannot force member states to take action.

common_errors.wrong: the UN was founded after World War I
common_errors.correct: The League of Nations was founded after WWI (1920). The United Nations was founded after WWII (1945) as a more effective successor.

common_errors.wrong: all UN decisions are binding on member states
common_errors.correct: Only UN Security Council resolutions are binding. General Assembly resolutions are recommendations and are not legally enforceable.

common_errors.wrong: every country in the world is a member of the United Nations
common_errors.correct: While 193 countries are UN members, some entities are not, such as the Vatican City (which has observer status) and some disputed territories.

facts.statement: A community is a group of people who live, work, or share common interests in the same area or have a shared identity
Culture includes the beliefs, customs, arts, foods, languages, and traditions shared by a group of people
Urban areas are cities with dense populations; suburban areas surround cities with lower density; rural areas are countryside with farms and open land
Diversity means having people of different races, ethnicities, religions, languages, and backgrounds in a community; it enriches society with varied perspectives
Traditions are customs, beliefs, or practices passed down from generation to generation within a family or culture
Every country has a unique national culture, but within each country there are also many regional and local subcultures
Heritage is something passed down from previous generations, including buildings, customs, language, and cultural practices
There are approximately 7,000 languages spoken in the world today; Mandarin Chinese, Spanish, English, Hindi, and Arabic have the most native speakers
Cultural exchange occurs when different cultures share ideas, traditions, food, music, and art with each other
Holidays like Diwali, Eid, Chinese New Year, Hanukkah, Christmas, and Kwanzaa are cultural celebrations observed by different communities around the world
Immigration is the process of moving to a new country to live permanently; immigrants bring diverse skills, cultures, and perspectives to their new communities
Indigenous peoples are the original inhabitants of a region; in North America, Native Americans lived on the continent for thousands of years before European colonization

common_errors.wrong: everyone in the same country has the same culture
common_errors.correct: Most countries contain many different cultural groups with distinct languages, foods, customs, and traditions. Cultural diversity exists within every nation.

common_errors.wrong: rural areas are less important than urban areas
common_errors.correct: Rural areas play a vital role in society, providing food production, natural resources, and open spaces. Both rural and urban communities are essential.

common_errors.wrong: traditions never change over time
common_errors.correct: Traditions evolve as communities change, adapt to new circumstances, and blend with other cultures. Some traditions are modified while preserving their core meaning.

common_errors.wrong: diversity only refers to race
common_errors.correct: Diversity encompasses race, ethnicity, religion, language, gender, age, ability, socioeconomic status, and many other aspects of human identity.

facts.statement: The four cardinal directions are north, south, east, and west; intermediate directions include northeast, northwest, southeast, and southwest
A compass rose on a map shows the cardinal and intermediate directions
A map legend (or key) explains what the symbols, colors, and lines on a map represent
A map scale shows the relationship between distances on the map and actual distances on Earth
There are seven continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia (Oceania), Europe, North America, and South America
There are five oceans: Pacific (largest), Atlantic, Indian, Southern (Antarctic), and Arctic (smallest)
The equator is an imaginary line around the middle of the Earth at 0 degrees latitude, dividing it into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres
Latitude lines run east-west (horizontally) and measure distance north or south of the equator; longitude lines run north-south (vertically) and measure distance east or west of the Prime Meridian
The Prime Meridian is an imaginary line at 0 degrees longitude running through Greenwich, England, dividing the Earth into Eastern and Western Hemispheres
A globe is a spherical model of Earth that shows the true shape and relative sizes of continents and oceans; flat maps always involve some distortion
Asia is the largest continent by both area and population; Australia (Oceania) is the smallest continent by area
A physical map shows natural features like mountains, rivers, lakes, deserts, and plains; a political map shows boundaries between countries, states, and cities

common_errors.wrong: north is always up and south is always down
common_errors.correct: North is the direction toward the North Pole and south toward the South Pole. On most maps, north is placed at the top by convention, but this is a choice, not a rule.

common_errors.wrong: flat maps show the Earth accurately
common_errors.correct: All flat maps distort the Earth's surface because a sphere cannot be perfectly represented on a flat surface. Different map projections minimize different types of distortion.

common_errors.wrong: the equator goes through the United States
common_errors.correct: The equator passes through South America, Africa, and Asia. The United States is entirely in the Northern Hemisphere, well north of the equator.

common_errors.wrong: Africa is a country
common_errors.correct: Africa is a continent containing 54 independent countries including Nigeria, Egypt, South Africa, Kenya, and many others.

common_errors.wrong: latitude and longitude are the same thing
common_errors.correct: Latitude lines run east-west and measure north/south position (0 at equator). Longitude lines run north-south and measure east/west position (0 at Prime Meridian). Together they pinpoint any location.

facts.statement: A democracy is a form of government where citizens have the power to choose their leaders through free and fair elections
The United States government has three branches: legislative (Congress makes laws), executive (President enforces laws), and judicial (courts interpret laws)
The US Constitution is the supreme law of the land, establishing the framework of the government and protecting citizens' rights
The system of checks and balances ensures that no single branch of government becomes too powerful; each branch can limit the powers of the others
Congress is the legislative branch consisting of two chambers: the Senate (100 members, 2 per state) and the House of Representatives (435 members, based on state population)
The Bill of Rights is the first ten amendments to the US Constitution, guaranteeing freedoms including speech, religion, press, assembly, and the right to bear arms
Local government includes mayors, city councils, and county boards that manage local services like schools, police, fire departments, and road maintenance
The President of the United States serves a four-year term and can serve a maximum of two terms (10 years total under special circumstances)
The Supreme Court is the highest court in the United States, consisting of nine justices appointed for life by the President with Senate confirmation
A monarchy is a form of government where a king or queen serves as head of state; a constitutional monarchy (like the United Kingdom) limits the monarch's power through a constitution and parliament
A dictatorship is a form of government where one person or a small group holds absolute power without the consent of the governed and restricts individual freedoms
The Federalist system divides power among local, state, and national levels of government, each with specific responsibilities and authority

common_errors.wrong: the President makes all the laws
common_errors.correct: Congress (the legislative branch) makes laws. The President can sign bills into law or veto them, and can propose legislation, but cannot create laws alone.

common_errors.wrong: a democracy and a republic are the same thing
common_errors.correct: In a direct democracy, citizens vote on all laws. In a republic (like the US), citizens elect representatives to make laws on their behalf. The US is a democratic republic.

common_errors.wrong: the Constitution has never been changed
common_errors.correct: The Constitution has been amended 27 times. The first 10 amendments (the Bill of Rights) were added in 1791, and the most recent (27th) was ratified in 1992.

common_errors.wrong: only the federal government has power in the United States
common_errors.correct: The US has a federal system where power is shared between the national (federal) government and state governments. States have their own constitutions, laws, and elected officials.

facts.statement: Needs are things required for survival (food, water, shelter, clothing); wants are things desired but not essential (toys, games, vacations)
Goods are physical products that can be bought and sold (books, food, clothing); services are actions performed for others (teaching, healthcare, haircuts)
A producer makes or provides goods and services; a consumer buys or uses goods and services
Supply is the amount of a product available for sale; demand is how much consumers want to buy; prices generally rise when demand exceeds supply
A budget is a plan for how to spend and save money; it helps people and organizations manage their finances
Taxes are required payments to the government used to fund public services like schools, roads, police, fire departments, and the military
Scarcity means that resources are limited while human wants are unlimited; all economic decisions involve trade-offs because of scarcity
An opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative given up when a choice is made; for example, choosing to buy a book means you cannot spend that money on a game
International trade allows countries to specialize in producing goods they can make most efficiently and import goods from other countries
Saving money in a bank account earns interest, which is money the bank pays you for letting them use your money
Inflation is the general increase in prices over time, which reduces the purchasing power of money
Entrepreneurship is the process of starting and running a new business; entrepreneurs take financial risks in hopes of making a profit
Natural resources are materials from the Earth that people use, including water, minerals, timber, and fossil fuels; renewable resources can be replenished, while nonrenewable resources cannot

common_errors.wrong: money has always existed
common_errors.correct: Before money, people used a barter system (trading goods directly). Coins were first used around 600 BCE in ancient Lydia (modern Turkey). Paper money came later.

common_errors.wrong: printing more money makes everyone richer
common_errors.correct: Printing more money without increasing goods and services causes inflation (prices go up), which means each dollar buys less. The total wealth does not increase.

common_errors.wrong: needs and wants are the same thing
common_errors.correct: Needs are essentials for survival (food, water, shelter). Wants are things you desire but can live without (video games, designer clothes). Distinguishing them is key to budgeting.

common_errors.wrong: trade only happens between countries
common_errors.correct: Trade happens at all levels: individuals trade with stores, businesses trade with each other, cities trade with nearby areas, and countries trade internationally.

facts.statement: A citizen is a person who is a legal member of a country; citizenship grants both rights (like voting) and responsibilities (like obeying laws)
In the United States, citizens can gain citizenship by being born on US soil, having US citizen parents, or through the naturalization process
Civic responsibilities include voting in elections, serving on a jury when called, obeying laws, paying taxes, and staying informed about community and national issues
The right to vote in the US is guaranteed to citizens age 18 and older, regardless of race, gender, or wealth
Community service and volunteering are ways citizens can help improve their communities through actions like cleaning parks, helping at food banks, or mentoring younger students
The Pledge of Allegiance is a statement of loyalty to the United States and its flag, often recited in schools and at public events
Freedom of speech, protected by the First Amendment, allows citizens to express opinions, but it does not protect threats, fraud, or incitement to violence
Civic participation can include voting, contacting elected officials, attending town meetings, peaceful protest, and joining community organizations
The rule of law means that all people and institutions, including the government, are subject to and accountable under the law
Taxes fund public goods and services that benefit everyone, including public schools, roads, libraries, parks, police, and fire protection

common_errors.wrong: only adults have civic responsibilities
common_errors.correct: Children and teens also have civic responsibilities including following rules, being respectful community members, staying informed, and volunteering. Many of these build habits for adult citizenship.

common_errors.wrong: voting is the only way to participate in democracy
common_errors.correct: Citizens can participate through contacting representatives, attending public meetings, peaceful protest, serving on juries, volunteering, and running for office.

common_errors.wrong: freedom of speech means you can say anything without consequences
common_errors.correct: The First Amendment protects citizens from government censorship. However, speech that involves threats, fraud, or incitement to violence is not protected, and private entities can set their own rules.

common_errors.wrong: you have to be rich to run for public office
common_errors.correct: While campaigns can be expensive, many elected officials come from modest backgrounds. Public financing, small donations, and grassroots organizing help diverse candidates run for office.
